title: Relative acyclic direct image for proper finite-presentation diagrams
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $U\to S$ and $V\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] morphisms of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Let $f:U\to V$ be a proper $S$-morphism. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and flat over $S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$, put $U_v=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and let $\mathcal F_v$ be the tensor pullback of $\mathcal F$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume that $U_v$ has Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $H^1(U_v,\mathcal F_v)=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, of finite presentation and flat over $S$, and $R^1f_*\mathcal F=0$. For every $a:S'\to S$, set $U'=U\times_SS'$, $V'=V\times_SS'$, let $a_U,a_V$ be the projections and $f':U'\to V'$ the induced morphism. The canonical degree-zero base-change map $a_V^*f_*\mathcal F\to f'_*a_U^*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. If, in addition, each $\mathcal F_v$ is generated by its global sections, meaning that $\bigoplus_{s\in H^0(U_v,\mathcal F_v)}\mathcal O_{U_v}\to\mathcal F_v$, with component $1\mapsto s$, is surjective, then the adjunction evaluation $f^*f_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is surjective. Here $R^i f_*$ is the right derived functor of structure-module direct image [pqf-def-cohomology].

source.place: Corollary 1.5, printed p.167, conditions (1),(2) and conclusions (i)--(iv). proof.text: Work over an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, and then over an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $V_{S_0}$. Put $X=f^{-1}W$ and $h=f|_X$. Higher direct images restrict by [lem-pc-sections-open-base-change]. A fibre of $h$ is of finite type over its residue field; apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] on its affine charts to pass from its geometric dimension bound to its ordinary dimension bound. Hence [lem-sfb-proper-quasicoherent-fibre-dimension-vanishing] gives $R^qh_*H=0$ for every quasi-coherent $H$ and $q>1$. Also $K=Rh_*\mathcal F|_X$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Here $X$ is proper over affine $W$, hence quasi-compact and separated, so the hypotheses for top-degree base change apply locally even if $S$ is not quasi-compact. Properness survives these restrictions and base changes by [lem-pc-proper-base-change].

By [lem-sfb-proper-top-cohomology-finite] with $d=1$, $N=R^1h_*\mathcal F|_X$ is of finite type. By [lem-sfb-top-degree-base-change], its tensor fibre at each geometric point $v$ of $W$ is $H^1(X_v,\mathcal F_v)=0$. For an ordinary point $w$, the vector space $N_w/\mathfrak m_wN_w$ therefore becomes zero over an algebraic closure of $\kappa(w)$; a basis of a vector space remains linearly independent after field extension, so that vector space was zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] in the local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ to get $N_w=0$. Thus $N=0$, and gluing over $W$ gives $R^1f_*\mathcal F=0$. The same top-degree comparison gives $R^1h'_*\mathcal F'=0$ after EVERY $W'\to W$, for the ordinary pullback $\mathcal F'$, and clause (a) gives vanishing above degree one.

source.place: Tags 0EX3 and 0EX4; agent Nakayama argument, with the finiteness checked before its use.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover of $X$ and its finite alternating Cech complex $C^\bullet$ for $\mathcal F|_X$. By [lem-pc-cech-resolution] and [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech], it computes $Rh_*\mathcal F|_X$ on affine $W$. It is bounded in degrees $0,\ldots,t$. Every intersection in this cover is affine: it is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of the separated morphism $X\to W$ inside a product of affine opens over affine $W$. Thus each term, a finite direct sum of sections on such intersections, is $R$-flat by [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. A finite sum is flat since tensoring decomposes into the finite sum of the exact tensor functors. Steps 1--2 give $H^q(C)=0$ for $q>0$, and $H^0(C)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$.

source.place: lemma-base-change-complex; agent use of the finite Cech model with base R, without assuming f is flat.

proof.text: Write $Z_i=\ker(C^i\to C^{i+1})$. Start with $Z_t=C^t$ (and set $C=0$ if $X$ is empty). Because $H^{i+1}(C)=0$, for $0\leq i<t$ there are short exact sequences $0\to Z_i\to C^i\to Z_{i+1}\to0$. Descending induction using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ses-kernel-flat] proves each $Z_i$ is $R$-flat, in particular $H^0(C)=Z_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] each displayed sequence stays exact after tensoring with any $R$-module $M$. Inductively its injection $Z_{i+1}\otimes_RM\to C^{i+1}\otimes_RM$ identifies the kernel and image of the next differential. Therefore $H^0(C)\otimes_RM\to H^0(C\otimes_RM)$ is an isomorphism and $H^q(C\otimes_RM)=0$ for $q>0$. This includes the one-term complex, where the assertions are immediate.

source.place: lemma-base-change-complex; agent explicit descending induction for the bounded flat Cech complex.

proof.text: For any affine $S'_0=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S_0$, use [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech] on $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its term maps identify $C\otimes_RR'$ with the Cech complex of the ordinary pullback on $X\times_RR'$: on an affine chart a quasi-coherent module is an associated module, whose tensor pullback has sections $M\otimes_RR'$ by [new-p4-locally-quasicoherent-affine-pullback-sections]. On degree zero step 4 gives $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_RR'\cong\Gamma(X\times_RR',\mathcal F')$. This is the specified comparison, since each term sends $s\otimes r'$ to $r'a_U^*s$. Over $W'=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR')$, its source also equals $\Gamma(W,f_*\mathcal F)\otimes_B(B\otimes_RR')$. The comparison is consequently an isomorphism of quasi-coherent sheaves, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. Such affine charts cover every $S'\to S$, and the formula on pure tensors agrees on restrictions, so the canonical maps glue. Step 4 also says the sections of $f_*\mathcal F$ on each $W$ are $R$-flat; [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] proves flatness over $S$.

source.place: lemma-base-change-complex; agent degree-zero comparison and gluing on affine charts.

proof.text: It remains to prove finite presentation, which does not follow just from finite type over an arbitrary ring. Still take $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$, but now use all of $V_{S_0}$ and $U_{S_0}$. Set $L=Rf_*\mathcal F$ there. It belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_V)$ by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] and is concentrated in degree zero by steps 1--2 (negative cohomology is zero for the right derived functor of a left exact functor on a degree-zero module). For every perfect $E$ on $V$, [lem-pc-derived-pullback-perfect] makes $Lf^*E$ perfect on $U$. Projection formula [lem-pc-projection-formula] and composition [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] identify the derived objects $R\Gamma(V,E\otimes^L L)\cong R\Gamma(U,Lf^*E\otimes^L\mathcal F)$. Both scheme morphisms involved are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; no Noetherian composition lemma is being used. The perfect test E belongs to D_QCoh by [lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent], as required by the projection formula.

source.place: Tag 0GES, perfect tensor tests; agent verification of the derived test objects using projection and composition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image] to $U_{S_0}\to S_0$, the perfect factor $Lf^*E$, and the bounded complex $\mathcal F[0]$. This morphism is of finite presentation, $\mathcal F$ is finitely presented and $S_0$-flat, and its support is proper over $S_0$ because $U_{S_0}$ is proper. Thus the right hand side of step 6 corresponds to a perfect object on $\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-pc-perfect-affine-module-preimage], its module-derived preimage is pseudo-coherent; the quasi-inverse in [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] is precisely $R\Gamma$, so it is the pseudo-coherent object of $D(R)$ required in the test. Since $V_{S_0}\to S_0$ is separated, flat and finitely presented, [lem-sfb-perfect-tests-detect-pseudocoherence] applies and proves $L$ pseudo-coherent on $V_{S_0}$. Now [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-top-cohomology-fp] at $n=0$ proves $f_*\mathcal F=H^0(L)$ finitely presented. This is local over $S$, so proves the global assertion. Here [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] makes the support closed, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes its reduced closed subscheme proper over S_0.

source.place: Tags 0GES and 09UU, with perfect.tex Tag 0A1H; cohomology.tex Tag 08DN(2). Agent application checking every base-flat hypothesis.

proof.text: For the optional generation assertion we need surjectivity of the map to fibre sections, not degree-zero base change along arbitrary $V'\to V$. Fix $w\in W$ and base change $h$ to $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$. The localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] identifies its degree-zero direct image with the localization of $h_*\mathcal F$, and its $H^1$ is zero. Write $A=\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $I=\mathfrak m_w$, $X_T=X\times_WT$, and $F_T$ for the ordinary pullback. By [lem-sfb-top-degree-base-change], $H^1(X_T,F_T\otimes h_T^*\widetilde I)=H^1(X_T,F_T)\otimes_AI=0$, and $H^2(X_T,H)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $H$. Sheaf quasi-coherence here can be checked on affine presentations: tensor products are associated tensors, and kernels and images are associated kernels and images by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact].

source.place: Tag 0EX3(b); agent local tensor calculation for the evaluation clause.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the image of $F_T\otimes h_T^*\widetilde I\to F_T$ and $P$ its kernel. They are quasi-coherent. The long exact cohomology sequence [pqf-def-cohomology] and step 8 give $H^1(X_T,J)=0$, since the adjacent groups $H^1(X_T,F_T\otimes h_T^*\widetilde I)$ and $H^2(X_T,P)$ vanish. If $i:X_w\hookrightarrow X_T$ is the closed fibre, then $F_T/J=i_*F_w$: on an affine chart it is the equality $M/IM=M\otimes_A(A/I)$. The same long exact sequence for $0\to J\to F_T\to i_*F_w\to0$ yields a surjection $H^0(X_T,F_T)\to H^0(X_w,F_w)$, using only the definition of direct-image sections to identify $H^0(X_T,i_*F_w)$. The target is killed by $I$, so the canonical map $(f_*\mathcal F)\otimes\kappa(w)\to H^0(U_w,\mathcal F_w)$ is surjective. Extending scalars to an algebraic closure $\Omega$ preserves this surjection, and [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] over the field identifies its target with $H^0(U_v,\mathcal F_v)$.

source.place: Tag 0EX3; agent two short-exact-sequence argument lifting sections to the closed fibre.

proof.text: Assume the geometric fibre modules are globally generated. The tensor pullback of the adjunction evaluation $f^*f_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ to $U_v$ is the composite of the surjection from step 9, tensored with $\mathcal O_{U_v}$, and the global-section evaluation of $\mathcal F_v$, hence is surjective. It is this composite because [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] defines the adjunction on sections, sending $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_{U_v}$. Let $Q$ be the cokernel on $U$. It is of finite type as a quotient of the finitely presented module $\mathcal F$. For any $u\in U$, put $w=f(u)$. The pullback of $Q$ to $U_w$ becomes zero after extension to $\Omega$; tensor with a field extension detects zero by the basis argument, hence its stalk at $u$ is zero. Thus $Q_u/\mathfrak m_wQ_u=0$, where the ideal is extended to $\mathcal O_{U,u}$. This ideal is contained in the maximal ideal of that local ring, so $Q_u/\mathfrak m_uQ_u=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] to the finite module $Q_u$ to conclude $Q_u=0$. All stalks vanish, so the evaluation is surjective.
